The future of AI and compute runs on light. At Sivers Semiconductors we're making that possible.

Sivers CEO @VickramVathulya recently joined @sallywf on @eetimes "AI with Sally podcast" to discuss Sivers' high-performance #photonics and #wireless solutions, along with the company's technology, manufacturing and business strategies.

From enabling greater efficiency in AI data centers to advancing next-generation connectivity, tune in as Vickram shares his perspective on where the industry is headed and the role Sivers is playing in this evolution.

🎧 Listen to the full conversation: https://www.eetimes.com/podcasts/enabling-ai-at-the-speed-of-light/
#SiversSemiconductors #AIInfrastructure #Photonics #OpticalConnectivity #Semiconductors

I found the technical discussion helpful, but investor messaging to be way too conservative.

If you look at how $NVDA CEO describes CPO, Jensen states scale up is increasing optical volumes by 15x. $LITE and $COHR are quantifying that by describing $5-$20B agreements spanning 3-5 years out.

Having this question, and not talking about Ayar, O-Net, Poet, or ELS partnerships. Then redirecting the question to near term pluggables seems off.

The vision also needs work, “communications and sensing” semi company is very unexciting.

It’s technically true, but there’s no vision being communicated on being the next $40B optical giant or what Sivers is going to be in the next 5 years that would attract long term holders.

The core valuation Sivers gets is from optical opportunities, I also personally disagree that it’s helpful to loop back to former cellular relationships when talking about future $GFS volumes

I disagree when you portray the company as “small” when Sivers 100m CW DFB capacity is coming online, alongside large foundry partners.

Which is a material % of the world’s annual laser capacity.

Investors want to hear about future economic opportunities and how you fill the gap with more qualifications during a bottleneck.

Sivers has a tremendous opportunity for CPO/NPO/Pluggables but I’m afraid it’s not being communicated properly. 

It’s understandable here since EETimes is more technical oriented, but I hope this messaging gets communicated better in the next earnings call.

It’s time to put all the pieces together, the early tests to see how crazy it was to build a vehicle this size, the suborbital hops to practice subsonic maneuvering, the first real booster, expendable flight tests, trips to the Indian Ocean, and last flight with payload to orbit. We are one step away from the full mission, and that step is the double catch.

We will try for the first time on flight 15. I don’t think and of us can promise it will work the first time, but getting here feels like a turning point. I still feel like there’s so much to review (and we will be doing that continuously between now and launch) but when I take a moment to stop and think about it, it is overwhelmingly exciting. This is the rocket that will build a human civilization on another planet.

text:
I have been talking with, and consoling Tesla Cybertruck fans.

Truth is I am jealous of every one of them.

I got to drive one for a day around Las Vegas, Nevada. 

Was on a curvy road with no traffic. 

So I opened it up.

Was like driving a space craft.

Bulletproof.

The best tech.

Innovation out the wazoo.

It is the best vehicle on the road.

By far.

I couldn’t convince my wife to like the design and I consider that one of my many moral failures.

It is a day of grief and embarrassment.

But @elonmusk learned a lot.

Someday he will come out with a family of vehicles rethought for autonomy.

Right now there is a ton of unsatisfied demand in San Francisco for the Cybercab which is where my eight-year-old robot is driving me to go see @stash_pomichter’s new robot-building factory.

But all this was put in perspective for me by @JohnNosta’s death.

His items showed up in my feed literally every day for many years.

I am still processing this news.

Let’s just say I am glad the car is driving. I talked with him in many space. Can’t believe he is gone.

This loss is 1000x worse.

Just can’t believe it. Back to the triangle mobile.

I will always take a ride in a Cybertruck.

The owners are all cultural revolutionaries.

Took on a ton of hate and turned it into love for triangles.

Oh and @teslaownersSV I will always be in your debt for letting me drive yours. Seen here in front of my house.

There is a future in robots.

 Cybercab is better for San Francisco.

Now gotta sell that to Democrats who want to eviscerate Elon and say so on their shows.

Our story is we talk about lives saved and interviews with people in the street.

They will tell you. They want Robotaxi.

From inside a @Waymo (I interview Waymo riders to learn about how the consumer is responding to autonomous vehicles/robotaxi and one woman told me about her rides in a Tesla. Or go to any tech company and ask around).

Everyone wants competition.

Even @elonmusk 

The dude lives for that.

San Francisco will go gold on the first day of  Cybercab.

Our city was built on gold. And I saw how deeply it changed Austin.

Actually the Cybertruck isn’t actually best on the road. Cybercab is.

More innovation is in the trunk @live_munro showed on its YouTube interview with Cybercab execs than in the entire Cybertruck.

It is a genius example of engineering excellence.

Cybertruck is too.

Wish more of us could have gotten one.

And I feel sorry for people who don’t have a Tesla. They don’t know what they are missing.
5 years ago

There are a lot of videos going around X on how to grow on social media.

Most of them are very zoomed out and look at the broader trends. If you’re just getting into marketing, I think that’s the wrong place to start.

You should be studying how to make one good video. Can you write a script, film a video, and edit it, so that it provides value and goes viral? If not keep trying over and over and over and over until you develop that instinct. 

The ability to just create valuable content on demand... That is your goal. 

Think of content like a startup. Just make a video people want. Once you find it, congrats you have CMF (Content Market Fit). Okay do it again and again and again and again and again and again improving every time. 

(btw this guys video was good. But if you don’t know how to make a good video, none of it matters)
